text:
Marathon Petroleum barely moved today, up just 0.2%, but the stock is up 10.5% over two weeks—a run that reflects the underlying volatility in crude oil and refining margins. Today's flatness comes after oil prices slid on news that the U.S. lifted sanctions concerns on Russian crude, which raised hopes of more global supply entering the market and eased some of the geopolitical premium that had driven prices higher earlier in the week. US crude is at $101.91 per barrel, down from the $110+ levels seen when Iran escalated attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz just days ago.

The two-week rally makes sense in context: refinery utilization is running at a healthy 93.5%, and the company benefits when crude prices spike on supply fears (like Iran's attacks), because refiners make money on the difference between what they pay for oil and what they sell refined products for. Now that oil has retreated on sanctions-relief news, that tailwind has eased, which is why the stock has settled into a holding pattern despite still being well above where it started the month.
